 Hon'Ble Anish Kumar Gupta, J. 
1.

Heard Sri Umesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri P.K. Srivastava,
learned Aga for the State.

2.  The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashing of the charge sheet dated 5.7.2014 as well as entire proceeding of Case No.17094 of 2017 arising out of Case Crime No.13 of 2013, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, Kanpur Nagar, District Kanpur Nagar, pending in the court of District & Sessions Judge,
Kanpur Nagar.
3.

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Thana, Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that opposite party no.2 was wife of applicant no.1.

Since there was matrimonial dispute between them, opposite party no.2 filed an application before the Superintendent of Police, Kanpur Dehat on 11.9.2012 making out allegations of demand of dowry, threatening, harassment and threw her out from her matrimonial house by the applicants.

Since no action was immediately taken on the aforesaid application submitted by opposite party No.2 to the Superintendent of Police, Kanpur Dehat, she filed a complaint case No. 635 of 2012 before the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2, Unnao making out identical allegations against the applicants on 19.9.2012.

entities.text: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2, Unnao
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: vide order dated 19.2.2013 applicants herein were summoned in the said complaint case filed by opposite party No.2.

Subsequent thereto, trial was conducted and opposite party no.2 made a categorical statement before the trial court that she was married to applicant no.1 and there was matrimonial dispute between the parties, due to which at the instigation of her family members she had lodged FIR against in-laws and her husband.
She categorically told before the Court that her husband and in-laws had neither made any demand of dowry from her nor they have tortured.

4. On the basis of aforesaid categorical statement made by opposite party no.2, the applicants herein were acquitted vide judgment and order dated 5.12.2014 by the trial court in the said complaint case.

In the meantime, on the application given by opposite party no.2 to the Superintendent of Police, Kanpur Dehat, FIR was registered on 21.1.2013 as Case Crime No. 13 of 2013 under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act at Police Station Mehrajpur, District Kanpur Nagar.
The matter was investigated by the police and charge sheet was filed against the applicants herein.
Since the applicants were not aware of the said case.
The charge sheet was prepared on 5.7.2014, but the same was filed before the trial court on 6.4.2017
, therein trial court took cognizance and issued summons against the applicants which were never served on the applicants.

Subsequent thereto,
non-bailable warrants were issued against the applicants.

When the applicants came to know about non-bailable warrants, thereupon, they filed the instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
seeking quashing of the entire proceedings of the FIR lodged for prosecution for same cause of action, for which they were already acquitted in the complaint case lodged by opposite party no.2.
5.
Vide order dated 7.7.2020, this Court issued notices to opposite party No.2.
Despite service of notice, there is no appearance on behalf of opposite party No.2 till date.

entities.text: Nand Kishor And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From perusal of record, it is evident that allegations made in the complaint by the opposite party no.2 are identical to the allegations made in the FIR, in which applicants were acquitted on the categorical statements made by opposite party No.2.
Thus, instant proceedings are nothing but the second prosecution for same cause of action.
Thus, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the case arising out of FIR as well as charge sheet against them.
7. Learned counsel for the applicants has also relied upon Article 20 of the Constitution of India and submits that no person can be prosecuted for more than once for the same cause of action.
8. Per contra, learned AGA submits that on the application given by opposite party No.2, FIR was registered on 21.1.2013.
Thereupon, the matter was investigated and after recording statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C., charge sheet was prepared.
However, charge sheet could be filed in the year 2017 only.
It reflects that thereafter trial court took cognizance of charge sheet.
Since after investigation, allegations have been found against the applicants, same cannot be quashed; and complaint case and FIR both should be clubbed and tried together.
Therefore, learned AGA opposed the quashing of further proceedings of the case.

9. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusal of record, it is evident that on the identical allegations, applicants have already been tried in a complaint case and were acquitted after analysis of the evidence led by the complainant vide order dated 5.12.2014.
The instant complaint was filed by the opposite party No.2 to the Superintendent of Police, Kanpur Dehat, on which later on, FIR was registered and the matter was investigated.
Though the charge sheet was prepared in the year 2014 but the same could not be filed before the trial court and the same was first time filed on 6.4.2017.
In the circumstances, Section 210 Cr.P.C. can not attract in this case.

Since the applicants have already been acquitted in the identical allegations made by the opposite party No.2 in the complaint case, the instant case is nothing but second prosecution of the applicants for the same cause of action which is unsustainable in law due to specific provision under Article 20 of the Constitution of India which prohibits second prosecution for the same offence.

10. In view of above, the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and entire proceeding of Case No.17094 of 2017 arising out of Case Crime No.13 of 2013, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, Kanpur Nagar, District Kanpur Nagar, against the applicants are hereby quashed.

(Anish Kumar Gupta,J.) October 6, 2025 P.P.
